svg.title: Neighbor-joining tree of 100 single cells from one breast tumor
svg.desc: Schematic of Navin et al., Nature 472:90 (2011), Fig. 2b. A tree drawn downward from its root at the top; the vertical axis is Euclidean distance from 0 to 5 and the horizontal axis is cell number from 1 to 100. Each leaf is one cell, placed at the depth measured on the published figure. The cells fall into four groups. Cells 1 to 47 hang close to the top, at a distance of about 0.7: 43 diploid cells and 4 pseudodiploid cells, which are the normal cells. Cells 48 to 71, the hypodiploid clone (24 cells), hang at about 2 and split off next. The remaining cells split at about 2.5 into aneuploid clone A (25 cells, at about 4.4 to 5.2) and aneuploid clone B (4 cells, at about 5.1 to 5.5). The branches that join the groups follow the paper's figure. Inside each group the paper's fine branching is left out and the group is drawn as a comb: one bar with a tooth down to each cell.
